main_text.p: in aurum verum naturale transfire, ad transmutationem metallicam oculis domonstrandam. Ne quis autem putet, antea infusum forte & admixtum argento plumbove aut Mercurio fuisse aurum, aut in ipso hæsisse sulphure, singula prius seorsim, si libet, per ignis & aquarum fortium criterea examinabit, quo certius sciat non aliunde, quam ex transformatione aurum hoc existere, per artis experimentum. Quod si quis autem sulphur per calcem nonnihil figat, indeq; aqua calida extrahat & infperfo aceto separet, ac deniq; quinta essentia Vini tartarisata ad rubedinem & ad oleitatem edistillata imbibat, majus operæ pretium secerit. Hæc commemoramus, ut principia naturalia metallorum proxima particulariter cognoscenda tradamus, & juris consultos in recepta sententia confirmemus & constabiliamus qui contra Angelum chymiam defendunt: quo quidem ablegamus & Principatus & Respublicas super hoc ne-

page.notes: Printed text is in italic throughout with roman words such as "Quod", "Angelum" and "Principatus" set in roman type; the italic and roman distinctions are not all marked. Marginal reference marks in the text ("indeq;", "deniq;") appear as small superscript signs and were transcribed as printed. Some ornament-letter and superscript forms are uncertain.
